summary: Firmware that turns a cheap ESP32 board into a voice AI chatbot that talks through MCP-connected models and tools.

heroCommands.command: Flash the beginner firmware using the guide at docs.xiaozhi.me

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: XiaoZhi is an MCP-based voice chatbot that runs on ESP32 boards. It streams audio with speech recognition, an LLM and text-to-speech, or end-to-end realtime voice models, and can control devices through MCP.
sixtySeconds.problem: Building your own voice assistant hardware is complicated. XiaoZhi gives ready firmware for many ESP32 boards and a hosted server so beginners can start quickly.
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for support across ESP32, C3, C5, C6, S3 and P4 chips, many supported boards, and both hosted and self-hosted server options.
requirements: A supported ESP32 board with microphone and speaker
For development: ESP-IDF v6.0.1 or later

overview: Beginners can flash prebuilt firmware without a development environment; see the Beginner's Firmware Flashing Guide. The firmware connects to the official xiaozhi.me server by default, where personal users can register and use the Qwen realtime model for free, per the README.
Developers build with ESP-IDF v6.0.1+ (release/v6.1 recommended). A breadboard tutorial for ESP32-S3 and a list of supported boards are in the docs.
You can self-host the server with community projects such as xiaozhi-esp32-server (Python) or a Java version. The firmware is MIT licensed.
limitations: Default server is a third-party service
